He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]]. ==Early life and career== George was born on 12 December 2003 and grew up in [[Monthey]], Switzerland.{{Cite web|url=https://miamihurricanes.com/roster/kyshawn-george/|publisher=[[Miami Hurricanes]]|title=Kyshawn George}} He was part of the team that won the Swiss U16 basketball championship in 2016.{{Cite web|url=https://miami.rivals.com/news/men-s-bb-miami-lands-commitment-from-kyshawn-george|website=[[Rivals.com]]|title=Men's BB: Miami lands commitment from Kyshawn George|date=20 April 2023|author=Benjamin, Marcus}} He later moved to France and played four years with the club [[Élan Chalon]].{{Cite web|url=https://woofradio.net/miami-freshman-guard-kyshawn-george-seizing-opportunity-with-louisville-up-next-tonight-its-just-me-getting-confidence-in-the-team/|publisher=[[WOOF (AM)|WOOF]]|title=Miami freshman guard Kyshawn George seizing opportunity with Louisville up next tonight: “It’s just me getting confidence in the team”|date=January 2024}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.lejsl.com/sport/2024/01/16/kyshawn-george-gagne-en-responsabilites-jermaine-love-efficace|newspaper=[[Le Journal de Saône-et-Loire]]|title=Kyshawn George gagne en responsabilités, Jermaine Love efficace|language=French|trans-title=Kyshawn George gains responsibilities, Jermaine Love efficient|date=16 January 2024}} George played mainly for the U18 team from 2019–20 to 2020–21 before then playing for the U21 team in 2021–22 and 2022–23, also spending time with the first-team squad in his last season. He averaged 11.1 points and two rebounds per game in 2021–22 and had 17.6 points, 6.5 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 2.4 steals per game with the team in 2022–23, being named first-team All-U21 Espoir Pro B. With the first team, he averaged 2.9 points and appeared in 16 games in 2022–23.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-miami-herald/141062929/|newspaper=[[The Miami Herald]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=21 April 2023|author=Kaufman, Michelle|title=Versatile Swiss guard added to UM's '23 recruiting class}} {{Open access}} George attended [[Lycée Emiland Gauthey]] in [[Chalon-sur-Saône]], France. He had a growth spurt in high school, going from a height of {{convert|5|ft|8|in}} to {{convert|6|ft|5|in}} and {{convert|6|ft|7|in}} by the time he entered college.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-miami-herald/141061246/|newspaper=[[The Miami Herald]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=10 January 2024|page=A22|title=Swiss import makes quick impact as first-year guard for Hurricanes}} {{Open access}} He committed to play [[college basketball]] in the United States for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]] in April 2023, being ranked a three-star prospect.{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/miami/basketball/canes-hoops-lands-recruit-from-switzerland|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Canes Hoops Lands Recruit From
